title: ConfinementManifest
description: cloister/confinement/v1 — the single declaration a runner compiles into kernel capabilities, digests as `confinementDigest`, and commits to a workload identity. Every dimension defaults to DENY; the manifest names only what is allowed, so an omitted block is a refusal and never an escape hatch.

version.description: Contract identifier. A runner that does not recognise this value refuses the manifest rather than interpreting it under a different version's rules.

fs.description: Filesystem dimension (README §2). Compiled to landlock_ruleset_add_rule on Linux and sandbox_init path allow-lists on macOS.

allow.description: Path prefixes the bundle may traverse. An empty array means every filesystem operation is refused — it is a valid, meaningful value, not a missing one.

network.description: Egress dimension (README §3), in two clauses: `allowHosts` names hosts reachable through the proxy, `connectLocal` names the single loopback port the workload may dial — typically that proxy. LISTENER control is deliberately NOT here; that is the `port` block, and the two are opposite directions.

allowHosts.description: Hostnames reachable for egress. An empty array, or an omitted `network` block, means no egress at all.

connectLocal.description: The single loopback TCP port this workload may connect(2) to, and may NOT bind. Single-valued for the same reason `port.bind` is: multi-port bundles publish v2. No 1024 floor, unlike `port.bind` — binding a privileged port is a privileged act, connecting to one is not. THIS DOES NOT AUTHENTICATE THE PEER: a loopback port is a shared host namespace, so the grant names which port may be dialled, not who is listening on it. A channel named this way needs its own authentication; `unixSocket.allow` gets peer identity from the filesystem, this gets it from the protocol or not at all.

port.description: Listener dimension (README §4). v1 is deliberately single-port; a multi-port bundle needs v2. An omitted block means the bundle MUST NOT bind any listener.

bind.description: The one port the bundle may bind. Privileged ports are out of scope in v1.

address.description: Bind address. Defaults to 127.0.0.1 when omitted, so exposing a listener beyond loopback is always an explicit declaration.

unixSocket.description: UNIX domain socket dimension (README §6). Compiled to a per-path socket grant on macOS; not available at the Landlock ABI this implementation targets, where a runner MUST refuse a §6 declaration rather than drop it.

allow.description: Socket paths the bundle may reach or serve. An empty array, or an omitted `unixSocket` block, means no UNIX socket access at all.

credentialSource.description: The one vault backend this bundle authenticates against for credential vending (README §5). Multi-vault fan-out is v2+. A bundle needing no credentials omits the field entirely.

FsEntry.description: One path grant: a bare string is read-only, an object carries an explicit mode. Read-only is the shorter form on purpose — the cheaper spelling is the safer one.

mode.description: Only `rw` is expressible. Read-only has no spelling here because it is the bare-string form; an explicit `"mode": "ro"` is rejected rather than silently accepted, so there is exactly one way to write each grant.

UnixSocketEntry.description: One socket grant: a bare string is connect-only, an object carries an explicit mode. Connect-only is the shorter form on purpose — as in FsEntry, the cheaper spelling is the safer one. `connect` requires the socket to already exist and grants only connect(2). `bind` grants bind(2), which CREATES the socket file, and withholds connect(2) — the serving half alone. `connect-bind` is both. A capability that dials a shim wants connect; the shim itself wants bind; only a process that must own an endpoint and dial through it wants connect-bind. A runner that cannot withhold connect(2) MUST refuse `bind` rather than widen it to connect-bind (§9 condition 5).

mode.description: Connect-only has no spelling here because it is the bare-string form; one grant, one spelling.

AbsolutePath.description: An absolute, canonical path prefix. Canonicalization (symlinks resolved, `.` and `..` collapsed) happens at manifest-compile time; a manifest containing a non-canonical prefix is rejected. The `..` exclusion is expressible here and enforced; symlink resolution is not expressible in JSON Schema and remains the runner's obligation.

HostPattern.description: A hostname, optionally prefixed with `*.` for a single leading wildcard. A wildcard anywhere else is rejected — `api.*.example.com` and `*api.example.com` are both refusals, because a pattern whose match set is hard to read is a pattern whose grant is hard to audit.

CredentialSource.description: A vault URI in one of the schemes `nono::keystore` validates. The enumeration is closed: a scheme this spec does not name is a scheme the reference validator will refuse, and accepting it here would move the refusal to a less obvious place.
